initial_requirements: European businesses need a Virtual Company Dossier service that helps them prove eligibility for public procurement across national borders. Economic operators should be able to identify required evidence, obtain and validate attestations, compile them into a dossier package, and submit it to contracting authorities. Authorities need to authenticate, receive, translate, and view the package while national criteria and evidence are mapped to shared European requirements.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What are the primary business goals for the Virtual Company Dossier service, and which stakeholder roles need to use or interact with it end-to-end?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
The main business goal is to let companies prove their eligibility for public procurement across borders without having to gather and resubmit the same evidence over and over again. It should make it easier to identify what evidence is needed, get it validated, bundle it into a dossier, and send it to the right authority in a usable form.
End-to-end, the main users are economic operators on one side and contracting authorities on the other. I’d also expect public sector or registry systems that issue and validate attestations to interact with it, and probably a support or administrative role for managing mappings, translation rules, and service configuration.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Could you describe the key functions the Virtual Company Dossier service must provide for each user type, from identifying required evidence through validation, dossier compilation, submission, and authority-side receipt and viewing?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
For economic operators, the service needs to help them discover what evidence is required for a particular procurement, collect or request the relevant attestations, validate them, and then compile everything into a dossier package they can submit. They should also be able to track what is missing or expired so they can complete the dossier correctly.
For contracting authorities, it needs to authenticate incoming dossiers, receive the package, translate or render the contents into something usable in their local context, and view the evidence in a clear way. On the backend, there also has to be support for mapping national criteria and evidence types to the shared European requirements so that both sides are talking about the same thing.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Which languages must the Virtual Company Dossier service support for dossier intake, translation or rendering, and authority-side review, and are there any specific multilingual or local-language requirements for the evidence and dossier package?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
I don’t know the exact set of languages yet, but it definitely needs to support cross-border use, so at minimum it has to handle the relevant EU and national languages involved in each procurement case. My understanding is that authorities should be able to receive and review dossiers in their preferred local language, or at least have the contents rendered clearly enough for review, even if some original evidence stays in its source language.
For the evidence and dossier package, I’d expect the original attestation to remain intact and the service to provide translations or normalized labels where needed, but whether those translations are legally binding or just for convenience still needs to be confirmed.

slots.name: project_goals
slots.value: Enable companies to prove their eligibility for public procurement across borders without repeatedly gathering and resubmitting the same evidence; help them identify required evidence, obtain validation, compile a dossier package, and submit it to the appropriate authority in a usable form.

slots.name: stakeholder_roles
slots.value: Economic operators, contracting authorities, public sector or registry systems that issue and validate attestations, and support/administrative users who manage mappings, translation rules, and service configuration.

slots.name: functional_needs
slots.value: Economic operators must be able to discover required evidence for a procurement, collect or request attestations, validate them, see what is missing or expired, and compile a dossier package for submission. Contracting authorities must be able to authenticate incoming dossiers, receive them, translate or render them for local use, and view evidence clearly. The backend must support mapping national criteria and evidence types to shared European requirements.

slots.name: business_rules
slots.value: National criteria and evidence types must be mapped to shared European requirements so both sides interpret the dossier consistently. Dossiers should surface missing or expired evidence to support correct completion before submission.

slots.name: data_entities
slots.value: Evidence, attestations, dossier package, procurement requirements, national criteria, shared European requirements, evidence types, missing/expired status, and translation/rendered dossier content.

slots.name: constraints
slots.value: Must support cross-border procurement use cases and align local/national evidence criteria with shared European requirements; authorities need authenticated receipt and usable local presentation of dossiers.

slots.name: quality_concerns
slots.value: Usability of dossier presentation for authorities, clarity of evidence status for operators, and consistency of translations/rendering across local contexts.

slots.name: boundary_conditions
slots.value: Handle cases where required evidence is missing, expired, or incomplete so operators can finish the dossier correctly before submission.

slots.name: interoperability_standards
slots.value: Shared European requirements and mappings between national criteria and evidence types must be supported, but no specific technical standard was stated.

slots.name: cross_border_identifiers
slots.value: Shared European requirements, national criteria, and evidence types used to map and identify evidence across borders.

slots.name: evidence_lifecycle_management
slots.value: Users must be able to identify needed evidence, collect or request attestations, validate them, track missing or expired items, and compile them into a dossier package for submission.

slots.name: submission_and_delivery_channels
slots.value: Economic operators submit dossier packages to contracting authorities through the service; authorities receive authenticated incoming dossiers and view them in a usable local format.

slots.name: translation_and_localization_requirements
slots.value: Contracting authorities need dossiers translated or rendered into something usable in their local context, with evidence presented clearly. Original attestations should remain intact, with translations or normalized labels provided where needed; the legal binding status of translations is still to be confirmed.

slots.name: supported_languages
slots.value: Exact languages are not yet defined; the service must support cross-border use and handle the relevant EU and national languages involved in each procurement case, including the authority's preferred local language where possible.

slots.name: translation_quality_and_legal_accuracy
slots.value: Translations or rendered content must be clear enough for authority review; it is not yet confirmed whether translations need to be legally binding or only for convenience.

slots.name: localized_presentation_formats
slots.value: Authorities should be able to receive and review dossiers in their preferred local language or in a clearly rendered form suitable for review, while keeping original evidence intact.

slots.name: authority_review_workflow
slots.value: Authorities authenticate incoming dossiers, receive the package, review the contents in a clear and locally usable format, and access the evidence needed for procurement evaluation.

abduction_history.surprising_fact: The service must translate or render incoming dossiers into a usable local format for contracting authorities, in addition to authenticating receipt and mapping national criteria across borders.
abduction_history.suspected_reason: This suggests authorities may operate in different languages and administrative formats, so the system likely needs a robust localization and presentation layer to preserve legal meaning while making evidence understandable and reviewable in each national context.

abduction_history.surprising_fact: The service must preserve original attestations intact while also providing translations or normalized labels for authority review, and it is still unclear whether those translations are legally binding or only for convenience.
abduction_history.suspected_reason: This implies a need to separate the authoritative evidentiary record from the localized presentation layer, so the system can support cross-border review without risking legal ambiguity or altering the original submitted proof.
